ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered screening of all founders, general partners, limited partners, signatories, and 25%-or-more UBOs against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Canadian Criminal Code terrorist entity list, OFAC SDN List for USD transactions, and domestic Quebec/RCMP watchlists. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates must be identified using enhanced due diligence and senior management approval before any registration step. All hits and negative news are documented in the AML dossier; if a hit is confirmed, the filing must be halted until legal clearance and, where applicable, FINTRAC reporting obligations are assessed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Registre des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Registrar official portal), available at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Quebec limited partnership must comply with the Charter of the French Language. The name must include a French-language distinctive element unless a statutory exception applies, and the legal form must be indicated in French as 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; the English form 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' may be used only as an additional trade designation where the Registrar accepts it. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters and translated into French by a certified translator for filing. The Registrar may refuse any name that is contrary to public order, that is offensive, that falsely implies governmental or regulatory endorsement, or that is confusingly similar to an existing enterprise name or protected trade mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives the Registrar's written reasons. The applicant may file an administrative review request with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of notification, attaching a corrected name proposal, a fresh name-search report, and, where applicable, written consent from the holder of a confusingly similar name. If the review is dismissed, the applicant may appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Quebec within 30 days of the review decision. While any appeal is pending, the applicant should file a new name reservation before the prior reservation lapses, as reservation validity is not automatically extended. Name refusals based on prohibited words may also be resolved by obtaining prior authorization from the relevant ministerial or regulatory body that administers the restricted activity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for registration purposes in Quebec only if the address is a physical street address in Quebec where legal process can be served and statutory books or records may be made available; post-office boxes and mail-forwarding-only facilities are not acceptable. For ISIC 4659 surplus commercial aviation parts distribution, a shared office, executive suite, or registered-agent service address can satisfy the registered establishment requirement, but the entity should maintain verifiable commercial substance, including transaction records, supplier contracts, and correspondence, because the Registrar and tax authorities treat a bare virtual address without local substance as a red flag.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-High: 15%-20% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months. This estimate is elevated due to the medium-risk aviation spares trading classification, non-resident ownership, and Quebec authorities' increasing use of establishment verifications and anti-money-laundering site checks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting together with the Department of Finance Canada and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). The Canadian foreign-exchange regime is governed by the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, the PCMLTFA (administered by FINTRAC), and Canada's Article VIII obligations under the IMF Articles of Agreement. There is no standalone central foreign-exchange administration authority requiring pre-approval of cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada maintains no exchange controls, no surrender requirements, no quantitative limits on inward or outward transfers, and no requirement for central bank authorization to remit dividends, distributions, or partnership profits. For a Quebec limited partnership, the sole frictions are tax-related: distributions to non-resident partners may attract Part XIII withholding tax at 25% statutory rate, subject to treaty reduction, and the Section 216 election may apply to certain rental-linked income; Quebec provincial withholding may also arise under the Taxation Act (Quebec). FX convertibility for CAD/USD/EUR clearing is deep and unrestricted at all Schedule I banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to surrender foreign currency to the Bank of Canada. Export receipts from aircraft parts sales may be held freely in CAD or foreign currency, and may be used offshore for working capital. The only applicable obligations are transactional reporting: FINTRAC large-value EFT reports and large cash transaction reports for amounts of CAN$10,000 or above, and bank-side balance-of-payments reporting under OSFI instructions; no exporter registration or export documentation filing is required for freely convertible proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, with strict legal constraints. Foreign electronic money institutions and digital cross-border payment providers are not authorized banks and cannot hold aviation-title-gated escrow balances or issue documentary letters of credit. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act, payment service providers must be registered with the Bank of Canada, and any foreign EMI serving a Quebec entity must also maintain FINTRAC money services business registration and a Canadian presence. Such platforms are viable only for incidental low-value supplier payments, currency conversion, and operating disbursements; they are not viable as primary treasury rails for surplus commercial aircraft parts distribution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory obligation exists for directors or partners to appear physically before a Canadian bank. PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance permit remote digital onboarding where identity verification uses independent and reliable technology. In practice, Schedule I banks classify aviation spares distribution as Medium-Risk Enhanced and normally require at least one in-branch or live videoconference interview with the natural-person signing officer and all ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the partnership, plus a verifiable Canadian business address for service. Fully remote account opening is achievable only with enhanced due diligence and an extended approval cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of beneficial ownership of the limited partnership, including aggregate partner interests and nominee limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of partners; notarized declaration of limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec; FINTRAC-compliant beneficial ownership schedule showing all 25% or greater owners; control-chain diagrams; sworn statutory declarations from the general partner; and current extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aviation-sector dual-use and sensitive inventory flags on surplus rotables and avionics
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canada Export Control List classification memorandum; item-level HS and ECCN mapping for NAICS 423860; Transport Canada and civil aviation sales authorization; supplier airworthiness certificates; end-user certificate for each consignee; and Incoterms annexes evidencing genuine aerospace supply-chain purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border wires to offshore repair stations, auction houses, and low-tax jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-way matched documentation per wire consisting of invoice, airway bill or bill of lading, and inspection certificate; underlying rotables sale contract; escrow flow diagram; source-of-funds statements; partnership capital ledger extracts; and auditable counterparty due-diligence file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow and holdback structures resembling unauthorized deposit-taking or trust activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Quebec counsel confirming that the escrow arrangement is an adjunct to the aviation sale and does not constitute deposit-taking under the Bank Act or Quebec trust rules; executed escrow agreement with a licensed Canadian bank or escrow agent; flow-of-funds ledger; and contractual release conditions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner concentration and tax-haven nexus triggering enhanced CDD and PEP-screen fatigue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS and FATCA self-certifications for all partners; tax-residency certificates; authenticated capital account ledgers; source-of-wealth documentation; Politically Exposed Persons screening no-match letter; and current Registraire des entreprises filing extract confirming good standing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Free-flow SWIFT wire (MT103 or MT202) denominated in CAD, USD, or EUR credited to the LP's Schedule I bank account; no Bank of Canada prior authorization, no minimum statutory capital for a Quebec limited partnership, and no conversion or surrender requirement. The remitter must denote the transfer as a capital contribution in the SWIFT remittance information referencing the partnership declaration, using ISO 20022 purpose code INTC (intra-company or group funding) where applicable; the receiving bank applies FINTRAC EFT reporting for amounts at or above CAN$10,000 and may require CRS, FATCA, and source-of-funds confirmation. Capital contributions are not subject to Part XIII withholding, which applies only to distributions and certain deemed benefits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers with UETR tracking for supplier disbursements; MT202 covers for correspondent-bank funding; commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 for large rotables and avionics purchases; and licensed escrow accounts releasing funds only on matched invoice-and-delivery evidence. Domestic CAD legs settle through Lynx Large Value Transfer System; USD legs settle via Fedwire or CHIPS; escrow rails maintain title-gating conditions before any release to the beneficiary. Every outbound wire at or above CAN$10,000 requires FINTRAC EFT reporting, and aviation disbursement files must carry the supporting airworthiness and end-user certificate suite.

Vanilla and barrier foreign-exchange options on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR purchased over-the-counter to hedge forecast aircraft-part trade flows
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD or EUR for matching long-dated partner capital and trade-finance liabilities

Non-deliverable forwards limited to residual exposure to non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies arising from surplus-part supply jurisdictions; CAD itself is fully deliverable and requires no NDF
FX forwards embedded in commercial letters of credit and escrow release schedules under an approved bank credit facility

Foreign currency deposits in USD and EUR operating accounts used as a natural offset hedge; as a non-financial counterparty below applicable OSFI margining thresholds, the LP is not subject to mandatory initial or variation margin on plain-vanilla FX derivatives with licensed bank counterparties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed solely by Québec partnership law on an ordinary limited partnership. Mandatory audit may be triggered by (i) the limited partnership agreement; (ii) lender, avionics customer, or aviation-escrow counterparty contractual requirements; (iii) public-securities regulatory conditions; or (iv) CRA/Revenu Québec review where books are deemed inadequate. For an ISIC 4659 aircraft-parts trading entity, contracts and escrow arrangements commonly require audited statements once annual turnover exceeds CAD 5 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook: Part II (ASPE – Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is the standard framework; IFRS is expressly permitted for private partnerships. Financial statements must be prepared on a consistent accrual basis and reconciled to the T5013 and CO-17 information returns.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Québec ALPE (Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises) requires that the annual declaration reflect all ultimate beneficiaries and significant-control persons as of the annual reference date. Since a limited partnership has no share capital, 'shareholding transfers' are reflected as changes in partnership interests; each such transfer must be updated in the partnership register and confirmed in the next annual declaration. For this ISIC 4659 aviation spares entity, annual confirmation must certify the current general partner, limited partners, and any person exercising control or significant influence over partnership decisions, including escrow and wire-transfer approval authorities.
